subject: grayWolf
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: gray wolf standing alert.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
I'm weighing whether to present this as targeted SEARCH/REPLACE edits or just rewrite the whole module, since changes touch most sections but a full rewrite risks being very long while edits risk exact-match failures.

I'll go with the full rewrite approach, planning out the geometry changes: adjusted skull and neck sweep scales, repositioned eye and muzzle landmarks, a multi-point catmull sweep for the muzzle with a downward break and tapered radii, a flattened nose shape, and an adjusted mouth seam box.

For the jaw I'm computing its frustum endpoints and radii so the top edge aligns just beneath the muzzle's bottom surface, keeping a small seam gap between them, while accounting for the muzzle's hexagonal cross-section having flat top/bottom faces that affect where that bottom edge actually sits.

Adjusting the jaw-to-muzzle gap to -0.097 and placing a dark seam box between them. I'll keep the cream chin blade but shift it down to -0.13, and rework the cheek wedges from simple spheres into tapered extruded shapes embedded into the skull that extend backward.

Adjusting the radius tapering, then placing cheek ruff blades slightly behind and refining the ear height ratio to 0.70, tweaking the outline points so the ears taper more decisively toward the tip.

I'm puzzling over why the outer ear renders pale cream instead of gray fur — it must be the inner ear's scaled-down cream mix bleeding through, so I'm tracing the normal vector calculation for the offset direction to check the geometry.

Now I'm deciding to make the outer ear paint explicit with a gray base and darker rim, and dial the inner ear to a smaller scale with a slightly darkened cream so the gray rim stays visible. Then I'm moving on to the brows, planning to recess them into the skull with a thicker sloping root using a wedge-shaped outline extrusion.

I'm checking that the eye and brow positions sit correctly against the skull ellipsoid's surface, adjusting the eye point and direction so the decal projects naturally onto the head shape.

Now I'm tuning the body proportions — reducing the vertical radius and tuck, shifting the body center down slightly, and adding shoulder blobs near the spine joint to emphasize the area above and behind the foreleg roots.

I'm checking withers blobs for overlap to create a continuous ridge, then adjusting hip blob position and scale to refine the haunch shape.

Now I'm simplifying the chest bib into one tapered pale shape so it reads better against the slimmer body, and setting up asymmetric stance offsets for each paw to stagger the fore and hind legs naturally.

I'm defining hind-leg target positions and contact points, then verifying the limb reach matches the segment lengths so the stride looks anatomically plausible. I'm also smoothing the fore limb's taper by adding an extra radius keyframe for a gentler profile along the chain.

Now I'm reworking the ruff fur, swapping the single ring of blades for two staggered rows of broader, sunken clumps for a fuller look.

I'm adjusting the ring radii to match the neck's taper more precisely—row 1 at roughly 0.19 with a slight sink, row 2 pulled in to about 0.15—so the blade roots sit properly against the cylinder shape. I'm also deciding to strip out the ruffHits cards while keeping cards wherever the roots would otherwise show, like around the chest.

I'll prune most ruffHits and tailHits cards, keeping a small reduced set of chestHits tucked under the chest with a wider minimum distance so they don't overcrowd. For the throat I'll just use a handful of ruff cards positioned under the neck, and since I'm rewriting the whole module anyway I can safely drop unused texture constants to avoid any unused-variable typecheck errors.

Still placing ridge and tail wedges...

I'm removing the banner assembly and sizing the rune stone to about 0.14 tall, scaling its outline proportionally and positioning it outside the wolf paws' silhouette around x=0.38, tightening the base width slightly to keep it clear of the other elements.

I'm placing two crystals outside the paw positions, around x=-0.34 to -0.36, double-checking they don't overlap the forepaw at x=-0.16, and keeping a small rock beneath them while confirming the banner removal also clears its associated variables.

Now I'm cleaning up unused imports and variables left over from removing the banner—dropping WOOD, GOLD, EMBLEM, grain, and frame since they're no longer referenced, while verifying gradient, cells, patches, and the joint/limb types are still needed elsewhere. I'm also confirming the base extrusion width and foot support stay consistent after the tightening, then moving on to reduce the charcoal tone in the fur.

For the fur shading, I'm adjusting the edge threshold curve and flank gray mix, cutting the streak contribution down, and reworking the underside color toward a cooler cream-gray instead of the warm cream. I'm tracing where the unwanted olive-brown tint is coming from—it looks like it's bleeding in from the fawn blend on the lower legs and body, since the underside height range overlaps with where that fawn gradient kicks in.

I'm also redefining the chest marking as a single tapered shape, using smoothstep functions on surface normals and height to narrow the marking width as it moves down the body, spanning from the lower body up to the throat.

Still refining head details...

I'm keeping the pale lip shading condition on the muzzle, and locating the neck joint position relative to the floor and skull scale. Now I'm setting up two reference points along the neck path to build a ring of blade-like elements, staggering two rows with offset starting angles around the neck's circumference.

Working out the stagger angles for row2 so items sit evenly without duplicating endpoints, then defining blade dimensions and tip counts per row, with color choices split between darker tones on top and cooler cream tones underneath.

I'm reusing the existing ridge function for the body with an added sink parameter, then setting up chest tuft placement filtered by position and surface normal, and positioning shoulder and withers blobs relative to the spine bone chain.

For the withers blob, I'm computing the vertical position by tracing the spine's radius curve at that parameter value, finding the top surface sits around y≈0.98, so I'm centering the blob near y=0.97 with scale rx 0.1, ry 0.07.

Checking the tuck transition across the spine from z=-0.42 to 0.48 gives a waist around t=0.3, z=0.0, which looks right, and the hip blob properly rides on the hind leg's hip joint. Now I'm filtering body sweep points for chest hits using a z>0.3 condition.

For coloring I'm applying a gradient to the tail sweep and fur to the cheek wedge as part of the head paint. For the muzzle I'm building a catmull-rom path with a radius function that tapers from 0.08 down toward the nose tip, adding a slight downward break near the end to give the nose a natural curve, then sweeping it with flat caps and six sides.

Now I'm working through the clearance between the muzzle's bottom surface and the jaw's top edge along the length of the snout, checking the gap at the tip versus near the base to make sure the jaw doesn't poke through or leave too large a visible seam, and adjusting the jaw's center y-offset and the muzzle's end y-value until the gap stays small and consistent.

I'll just accept a small gap and adjust the jaw endpoints: setting the start and end jaw heights so the middle gap narrows to about 0.0055 against the muzzle's underside.

I'm defining the jaw joint position and aim direction, then checking a seam box placement that might poke visibly out of the side as a dark band.

Removing teeth and tongue to simplify. Now I'm placing the eye and ear decal points, computing their positions relative to the skull's ellipsoid surface to verify they sit flush against it.

Working through the nose geometry now—placing the nose blob and highlight point at the muzzle tip, checking its extent against the muzzle's ellipsoid boundary, plus adding a darker tone near the nose end.

critic.text:
1. **Give the head more authority and separate it from the neck.** The wolf reads clearly, but the small skull flowing directly into the long neck weakens the Warcraft silhouette. Increase `skull` from `[0.15, 0.13, 0.155]` to approximately `[0.175, 0.145, 0.17]`. Taper the upper `neckSweep` radius from `0.15` to `0.13`, keeping the lower ruff broad. Reposition facial features onto the enlarged skull rather than scaling the entire head assembly. **Next render:** a substantial, intelligent head with a distinct brow, cheek and nape—not a narrow face at the end of a continuous wedge.

2. **Rebuild the muzzle and cheeks as connected anatomy rather than stacked primitives.** The close-up exposes a ruler-straight snout, rectangular lower jaw and hanging cheek bulbs. Shorten the muzzle endpoint from `hp(..., 0.34)` to about `0.30`; retain a broad root but give its bridge a slight downward break near the nose. Move the nose with it and flatten its depth to about `0.028`. Replace the two cheek spheres with tapered wedges embedded into the skull, extending backward into the cheek ruff. Shorten the `jaw` endpoint to approximately `0.285`, reduce its height to `0.025–0.03`, and bring it close enough to leave only a `0.003–0.005` mouth seam. Remove the isolated visible fang for this closed-mouth pose. **Next render:** one cohesive canine muzzle with a firm lip line, not a separate lower beak.

3. **Make the ears and eyes feel sculpted into the face.** Reduce `EKY` from `0.8125` to approximately `0.70`; keep the broad ear bases and notch, but taper the upper third more decisively. Give the outer ear a gray rim instead of allowing the pale inner-ear mass to dominate its front. The black brow extrusions currently read as raised bars: recess their lower edges into the skull and use a thicker, sloping root that merges into the forehead. Reduce `EYE` decal height from `0.064` to around `0.052`, reproject onto the resized skull, and remove `glow(eye, 0.2)`. **Next render:** compact wolf ears and focused amber eyes, with natural socket depth and no floating eyebrow appearance.

4. **Clarify the shoulder, rib cage and flank silhouette.** The side view has a fairly uniform barrel, while the pale chest hangs like a separate rounded bib. In `bodySweep`, increase the abdominal tuck from `0.035` to roughly `0.05`, reduce the final vertical radius from approximately `0.27` to `0.245`, and reduce the downward front shift from `-0.05` to about `-0.025`. Build the shoulder emphasis above and behind the foreleg roots instead of adding more hanging chest volume. Embed the hip blobs farther inward and reduce their vertical radius from `0.20` to about `0.175`. **Next render:** powerful withers and rib cage, a visible waist, and haunches that belong to the torso rather than resemble attached plates.

5. **Break the perfectly paired stance while preserving solid footing.** In the leg loop, offset one forepaw about `0.06` forward and the other `0.03` backward; stagger the hind paws by approximately `0.10` in depth. Apply each offset consistently to the chain endpoints, `paw()` placement and `contact`. Keep every sole at `FLOOR`. Recess the upper leg sweeps into their shoulder/hip masses and soften abrupt width changes around the knees and hocks through intermediate sweep radii. **Next render:** four readable, weight-bearing legs in three-quarter view and an alert, balanced animal rather than a mirrored display stance.

6. **Replace the scattered fur chips with a few rooted, directional masses.** The neck, spine and tail currently show little triangular scraps and stacked sawtooth strips, especially from behind. Remove most `ruffHits` and `tailHits` cards; retain cards only where their roots disappear inside the coat. Use fewer, broader `blade()` clumps, with roots sunk `0.025–0.035` into the supporting sweep and thicker bases. Arrange the ruff in two staggered overlapping rows flowing backward. On the tail, replace the repeated three-tip fans with five to seven larger alternating wedges following `tailPath`; eliminate the dangling cream fringe. **Next render:** a coherent heavy coat and bushy tail, with purposeful silhouette breaks rather than confetti or feathers.

7. **Let the wolf own the composition.** Remove the banner assembly: it is mostly hidden in the hero view, produces unexplained gold spikes in profile, and competes strongly in the back view. Reduce the rune stone’s height to approximately `0.14` and keep only two smaller ice crystals, positioned outside the paws’ silhouettes. Tighten the base width by roughly `10–15%`, preserving support beneath all feet. **Next render:** the face, chest and stance attract attention first; the snowy outcrop supplies context without becoming a second subject.

8. **Finish with larger, cleaner coat-color shapes.** In `FUR`, reduce the normal-driven charcoal coverage so the flanks remain visibly medium gray; reserve the darkest values for the saddle, nape and tail tip. Replace the olive-brown underside with a cooler cream-gray transition. Lower the `FAWN` blend strength from `0.75` to around `0.3` so the legs do not end in sharply defined brown socks. Reduce the small streak contribution and keep the chest marking as one connected tapered shape. **Next render:** a recognizably gray wolf with a strong dark saddle, pale throat and muzzle, and amber eyes as the principal color accent.
